analyst_view.overall: Early view: Frosinone are sixth and play an attacking, front-foot style under Alvini, though they lost 1-0 at Cagliari despite 29 shots and top scorer Raimondo went off injured. Bracaglia, listed as suspended, should have served his one-match ban at Milan the week before. Parma's Abdoulaye Ndiaye, sent off for denying a clear chance against Bologna, normally serves a one-match ban, which would fall on the Roma game, so he should be back here unless the ban is extended.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly higher: Frosinone have scored 2.7 a game at home, including 5-1 against Lecce, and their home games have averaged 3.7 goals. Parma's games are the lowest-scoring in the league, so I would not go much higher, and Raimondo's fitness matters.

corners.text: The site expects 11.2 corners, a high number that fits: Frosinone's games are the busiest in Serie A for corners at over 13, and Parma concede about 6.6 a game, the most in the league. Parma also take few corners themselves, so I stay with the number rather than going higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean lower because Parma's away games have averaged only about 1.6 cards, among the calmest of any team on the road. Frosinone's home games are higher, at almost four, so the lean is small.

shots.text: The site expects 37.8 shots, mostly Frosinone's. I lean lower: Frosinone's home games average about 36, and Parma's away games about 30, because Parma take only around eight shots a game away. Frosinone will shoot a lot, but 38 is high even for them.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. Frosinone's home games average over 12, while Parma rarely hit the target, at about three a game, so I stay with the number. Without Raimondo, Frosinone have been less clinical, as they showed against Cagliari's keeper Caprile.
